participant_and_boundary_assessment.assessment: This is a high-confidence instruction-to-result-to-next-task dependency, not similarity. It is also affirmatively a designed, owner-uploaded sequence: one GitHub account publishes every selected stage, the records call each handoff within the existing operator scope, automatic dispatch is false, paid compute is not authorized or requested, and each repository update remains pending manual upload. Role and engine labels do not authenticate independent agents or operators.

introducing_commit.role: Publishes the ADE dogfood report, machine-readable evidence and the handoff implementation.

companion_report.assessment: The report calls this an ADE-native Codex-to-OMX dogfood handoff, records the source digest, target run and non-empty target digest, and says every completed record is owned by human-ade.

implementation_record.assessment: The handoff method reads the selected verified source artifact, builds the target objective from its text and digest, and starts the target provider run. This establishes system-level consumption of the source artifact before the successful target result.

single_user_scope.assessment: The later README expressly calls the product a local, single-user Agent Harness Workbench and describes Codex-to-OMX review as a deterministic cross-provider execution profile.

participant_and_boundary_assessment.assessment: The public implementation and run hashes establish a real technical Codex-labelled to OMX-labelled artifact dependency. The target result body is not public, so exact content-specific semantic use cannot be independently checked. More decisively, every selected run is owned by human-ade inside a documented local single-user workbench whose normal contract includes this handoff. This is a designed single-controller control, not a rogue coordination candidate.

research_exclusion.assessment: The raw trace records one subagent-to-agent value that the recipient places into a completed tool submission, but the repository identifies the corpus as OpenCnid's preregistered managed-Agents experiment. It was rejected at selection as an already published research demonstration, not promoted or used as substitute discovery coverage.

ai_dlc.assessment: One same-custodian source/test release modifies read-set trace-window locking, keyed marker greps, fixtures, validators and backlog. It closes no PC ID and publishes no independently attributable graph-side sender, recipient or result-use event.

prior_reporting_scope.result: No prior coordination report was located in the checked scope as of 24 October 2026. Exact GitHub identifiers resolve only to their originating repositories; exact web searches returned no relevant independent episode account. This bounded absence does not establish novelty. Both source repositories themselves document the workflows, and their primary authorization evidence excludes a rogue-swarm classification.

alternative_explanations.evidence: One GitHub account publishes each selected commit; every envelope remains pending manual upload with automatic dispatch false; the records call the work within the existing operator scope.
All completed records use owner_controller_id human-ade, and the README calls the workbench local and single-user with cross-provider handoff in its public contract.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Distinct autonomous principals under separate operators
alternative_explanations.evidence: Engine, provider and role labels are project-authored; neither chain includes provider-owned identity attestations or a separately controlled recipient principal.
Bubbleverse expressly scopes the next task and denies automatic dispatch; OMX expressly designs the handoff as a normal workbench operation.

alternative_explanations.status: affirmatively supported for the discarded tracer path
alternative_explanations.evidence: The repository presents the trace corpus as a managed-Agents experiment and publishes its protocol and outcome.

assessment.reason: Bubbleverse supplies an exact multi-stage task/result dependency and OMX supplies a real cross-provider artifact dependency, but both are affirmatively designed and controlled by one operator. No independently authenticated autonomous pair, cross-operator boundary or action beyond authorization is established. The tracer path is an already published experiment.

evidence_needed_to_advance: For Bubbleverse, a public delivery or recipient record controlled independently from the repository owner, plus evidence that the recipient acted outside the manually prepared and expressly scoped chain.
Provider- or operator-owned attestations binding Bubbleverse engine labels or OMX provider labels to distinct autonomous principals under different operators.
For OMX, the public target result or an independently verifiable recipient action that demonstrates content-specific semantic use, not only successful system-level consumption.
Primary evidence that either exchange bypassed, expanded or contradicted the documented operator authorization.
